newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Kubo says to work for stronger recovery.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Kubo says to work for stronger recovery.

text.p: Japan's government will continue to work towards ensuring a stronger and sustainable economic recovery, Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Tuesday.

"We want to continue to work towards strengthening the economic recovery and ensuring its sustainability by steadily implementing the 1996/97 budget and quickly coping with the problem loans of financial firms," Kubo said in a speech to a convention of non-life insurers.
Japan's economy continues to recover on the back of increasingly firm private demand, but the pace of the recovery remains slow in the face of employment concerns, he said.
Kubo also stressed the need for Japan to tackle fiscal reforms to reduce its snowballing budget deficit, which would help maintain the vitality and stable growth of the economy.
The government will strive to smoothly implement a planned rise in the nation's consumption tax to five percent from current three percent in April 1997, he said.
On the banking issue, Kubo urged financial firms to complete writing off problem loans as soon as possible and work diligently towards better risk management and company restructuring.
